resources.string: The look of the Book That Reads You Back design. Off brings back the classic look.
Each one is off until you turn it on. Turning one off hides it; what it saved stays.
Back after a break: where you stopped and what came just before, in 20 seconds.
Before a chapter, guess the answers to a few questions; the text then answers them.
Marks the job each phrase does: claim, evidence, example, caveat.
Before you start: the whole argument in one line, a paragraph or a chapter map.
The book\'s ideas mapped to the terms of a field you know.
Read a chapter in full, lean, as claims only or in one line.
After a chapter, say what it said in your own words, then see what you missed.
Name what you want to understand; get the fewest chapters to read, in order.
Margin notes on what has been learned since the book was written.
Turn one idea into a small experiment this month, then check in two weeks later.
A few minutes a day on the ideas you are about to forget, across your books.
When you finish: the book in a few pages, from your recalls, misses and links.
A passage drawn as a process, a table or a loop.
Who\'s who, the timeline and the map, only up to where you are.
The front camera notices re-reads, drift and tiredness and offers help. It stays on this phone.
